resources.string: ROCKET ON PAD — NOT ARMED\ntap top panel to snooze
Warning. Rocket is on the pad and not armed.
Can\'t disarm while the rocket is in flight. Wait until it has landed.
Enter the password to connect to “%1$s”.
Another locator (ID %1$s) is on the air and is not being displayed. Connect to switch to it, or move to an uncontested channel.
Locator ID %1$s found. Enter its password to connect.
Channel is busy, but your link is clean.
Your channel (%1$d) carries your locator, as expected.
Your channel (%1$d) has a locator on it and none is connected — someone else is using it.
Channel %1$d has another locator on it — not offered.
Channel %1$d has %2$s on it — not offered.
Where the receiver listens. Point it at a channel a locator is already on — it does not move the locator. Picking a channel from a scan above applies straight away; typing one here needs Update.
Moves the connected locator, and the receiver follows it automatically. Use this when the channel is chosen for you; otherwise let the scan pick one.
%2$s is on channel %1$d — moving here would put two locators on one channel.
The locator is armed or in flight, so neither scan can run — either would leave the receiver deaf for up to a minute and a half. Disarm to scan.
Listens on the channels your locators were last seen on. Use this when a locator is powered up but nothing is coming through.
Listening on channel %1$d of %2$d — a full sweep takes up to about 90 seconds.
Connecting points the receiver at that channel, and takes effect straight away. Your locator stays where it is, and you will be asked for its password if the app does not know it yet.

Search all 64 channels appears once a shorter search has finished. It sweeps the whole band — up to about 90 seconds, during which the receiver hears nothing, and less when it finds locators along the way, since it moves on as soon as a channel answers — and is worth it when the locator is not on any channel the app knows to try, or when you are looking for one it has never met.
Nothing found anywhere in the band. Check that the locator is powered on and within range.
Search stopped. If you did not stop it, a command you sent to the locator did — the receiver has to be back on your channel to deliver it.
The locator is armed or in flight. Searching would leave the receiver deaf for up to a minute and a half, so it is refused until it lands and disarms.
The receiver is busy — a scan, a flight data transfer, or a command still on its way to the locator. Try again in a moment.
No response from the receiver. If its firmware predates locator search, update it — otherwise try again.
Names and channels here come straight off the air and are not password-checked. Recognition happens as usual once the receiver is pointed at the channel.
Candidates are listened to for a full second each, so an intermittent transmitter cannot hide between samples.
Moving to channel %1$d… the link drops briefly while both devices switch.
Could not send the channel change. Check the receiver connection.
The locator did not confirm channel %1$d. It has been left on its previous channel.
Could not check where the locator is — the receiver was busy. The receiver is on channel %1$d; use Find a locator.
Connecting to a result stops the scan — the receiver cannot keep searching and hold the channel you picked.
The locator did not respond, so nothing was moved. The receiver is still on channel %1$d — power the locator up and the link should resume.
Could not confirm where the locator is. The receiver is on channel %1$d — if the locator does not come back, use Find a locator.
Moves your locator to the chosen channel; the receiver follows automatically.
No locator connected, so this only re-points the receiver. Your locator stays where it is.

Every channel reads the same raised level — a transmitter close to the receiver, usually your own locator, spilling across the whole band. It does not favor any channel, so these are all equally good. Move the receiver away from powered locators for a sharper reading.

Every channel reads loud, which usually means a transmitter is very close to the receiver — check for another powered locator nearby. Move it away and scan again for a true reading. The channels below are still the least affected, and should be clean once it is moved.
The locator is armed. Scanning would stop telemetry for about eight seconds, and the channel cannot be changed while armed. Disarm first.
The receiver is busy — a flight data transfer, or a command still on its way to the locator. Try again in a moment.
Scan stopped so your command could reach the locator. Scan again when you are ready.
Scan stopped. The receiver is back on your channel and listening.
No response from the receiver. If its firmware predates channel scanning, update it — otherwise try again.
Measured where the receiver is. A channel that is quiet here may be busier at altitude.

No flight logs yet. One is recorded automatically when the app sees a rocket leave the pad, starting two seconds before launch detection. Nothing is recorded for a flight the app was not already receiving telemetry for.
%1$s will be removed from the phone. Anything already shared or saved elsewhere is unaffected.
Could not prepare the log for sharing.
Showing the first %1$d of %2$d rows. Share or save the log to read all of it.
This log is still being written. It can be shared now; more rows will follow.
